---
title: "Setup Guide"
subtitle: "Do this before the course — budget ~20 minutes"
---

::: {.callout-important}
## Please complete this *before* class
We're fully remote on Zoom, and setup problems are slow to debug for 30 people at once. Work through every step below and run the **[verification checklist](#verify-your-setup)** at the bottom. If something fails, note the error and bring it — we'll have a few minutes at the start for stragglers.
:::

You need four things: **git**, a **GitHub account** (with the `gh` CLI), **Claude Code**, and a working **terminal**. Here's each, by operating system.

## 1. A terminal

- **macOS:** open **Terminal** (Applications → Utilities → Terminal), or install [iTerm2](https://iterm2.com/).
- **Windows:** install [**Git for Windows**](https://git-scm.com/download/win) — it comes with *Git Bash*, which we'll use as the terminal. (Alternatively, use [Windows Terminal](https://aka.ms/terminal) + WSL if you already have it.)
- **Linux:** your existing terminal is fine.

## 2. Git

::: {.panel-tabset}
### macOS
Git ships with the Xcode command-line tools. Trigger the install:

```bash
xcode-select --install
```

Or via [Homebrew](https://brew.sh):

```bash
brew install git
```

### Windows
Installing [Git for Windows](https://git-scm.com/download/win) (above) also installs git. Use **Git Bash** as your terminal.

### Linux
```bash
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y git   # Debian/Ubuntu
```
:::

Then tell git who you are (use the email tied to your GitHub account):

```bash
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "you@example.com"
git config --global init.defaultBranch main
```

## 3. GitHub account + the `gh` CLI

1. Create a free account at [github.com](https://github.com/join) if you don't have one.
2. Install the **GitHub CLI** (`gh`) — it's the easiest way to authenticate and open pull requests:

::: {.panel-tabset}
### macOS
```bash
brew install gh
```

### Windows
```bash
winget install --id GitHub.cli
```

### Linux
See [cli.github.com](https://cli.github.com/) for your package manager.
:::

3. Log in — this also sets up git's credentials for pushing:

```bash
gh auth login
```

Choose **GitHub.com → HTTPS → Authenticate with a web browser**, and follow the prompt.

## 4. Claude Code

Claude Code is the agent we'll use — but note it's *an* agentic tool, not *the* agentic tool. Everything we practice (prompting, context files, the git review loop, skills) works the same way in [OpenAI's Codex CLI](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli), [Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli), and similar tools; only command names and config files differ. We standardize on one tool so the hands-on parts run smoothly.

Install it and sign in:

```bash
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
```

::: {.callout-note}
## No Node/npm?
Claude Code needs [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) (LTS). Install it first: `brew install node` (macOS), `winget install OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS` (Windows), or download from [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/). Then re-run the install command.
:::

Start it once from any folder to sign in:

```bash
claude
```

Follow the browser prompt to authenticate with your Anthropic account. You'll need an account with access to Claude Code — see [claude.com/claude-code](https://claude.com/claude-code) for current options.

## Verify your setup

Run each command. You should get a version number or sensible output — **not** "command not found."

```bash
git --version
gh --version
gh auth status
node --version
claude --version
```

Then confirm you can create and push a repo (this is the exact loop we'll use in class):

```bash
# make a throwaway repo, commit, and push it to your GitHub
mkdir agentic-warmup && cd agentic-warmup
git init
echo "# Warmup" > README.md
git add README.md
git commit -m "First commit"
gh repo create agentic-warmup --public --source=. --push
```

If that last command opened your new repo's URL (or printed it), **you're fully set up.** 🎉 You can delete the repo afterward with `gh repo delete agentic-warmup --yes`.

::: {.recap}
Setup complete when: `git`, `gh`, `node`, and `claude` all report versions; `gh auth status` shows you're logged in; and you successfully created + pushed a test repo.
:::

## Trouble?

| Symptom | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| `command not found: git/gh/claude` | The tool didn't install or isn't on your PATH. Reinstall; on Windows use **Git Bash**. |
| `gh auth login` won't open a browser | Choose "paste an authentication token" and follow [these steps](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_auth_login). |
| `claude` says not authenticated | Run `claude` (no args) and complete the browser sign-in. |
| Corporate laptop blocks installs | Bring it up in the setup window at the start of class, or use a personal machine if possible. |
